items.suggested_title: Hawaii water damage restoration: what island homeowners need to know before they call
items.notes: Island-wide gap: the url-plan covers water damage restoration per-city but has no Oahu or Hawaii-wide page, and 'hawaii water damage restoration' pulls 210/mo at KD 20 with a $21 CPC. Frame around what makes island losses different from mainland losses: year-round humidity collapsing the 24-48 hour mold window, salt-air corrosion on valves and angle stops, single-wall construction that wicks water, high-rise riser failures that cascade through units. Route readers to the per-city pages. Truth gate: no IICRC or license claims, no specific founding year, 'over 25 years' phrasing only.

items.suggested_title: Who is responsible for water damage in a condo: owner, neighbor, or the AOAO?
items.notes: Highest local-fit question in the whole fan-out. Urban Honolulu is condo country (Waikiki, Kakaako, Ala Moana, the Diamond Head Gold Coast co-ops) where one failed riser or supply line soaks the units below and pulls in AOAO coverage alongside the owner's HO-6. Explain the split between association master policy and unit-owner policy in general terms, and what documentation the association's insurer will expect. Keep it educational: state plainly this is not legal or insurance advice and that the governing documents control.
